pools._comment: Scrap roll. A fridge is mostly sheet steel and moulded plastic, with the control board's electronics rarer.

_comment: Secondary roll: what was left in the freezer. The only ice or snow in this world - the
garbage biome has no weather that makes either.
REAL ice, and it IS a water source - owner ruling 2026-08-12, made with that consequence
stated. Broken without silk touch on solid ground it leaves a water source block, and two
sources are infinite water, so this is a route to water that needs no Rain Collector and no
bucket. It shipped as packed ice for one commit on exactly that reasoning and was overruled:
"I know it creates a water source. Its fine gameplay."
What still holds is SCALE, which is why leachate_is_not_water is untouched. Water off a
fridge costs a Bulky Waste find, a prybar and a 1-in-4 draw; leachate answering yes to being
water would turn every pool on the map into a tap. A bounded route is a reward, an ambient
one is the end of the economy.
no_teardown_hands_out_a_free_water_source still guards every OTHER teardown, with this one
entry allowlisted by id - so the next water source has to be argued for, not absorbed.
Component roll, and the knowledge follows it. A fridge holds a compressor motor, a
refrigerant pump and an interior bulb, so which one you recover is a lottery - and whichever
comes out is the one you learn.
NO FILLER ENTRY, deliberately. You always get exactly one component; what you never get is to
choose which. That is what keeps a_component_teardown_always_yields_a_component true after the
owner's 2026-08-12 ruling that the lottery overrides the old one-object-one-component rule.
